Telegram Drive gives Ortho Tips a private cloud backup using a channel only you can see. Patient photos, radiographs, documents and records are copied there so a lost or replaced phone does not mean lost cases.\n\nLocal storage keeps working exactly as it does today. You can switch back at any time, and nothing is ever deleted when you switch.

• A Telegram account you already use.
• Your own API id and hash from my.telegram.org — free, takes two minutes.
• A network connection for the first synchronisation.

Ortho Tips never sends your credentials anywhere except Telegram itself, and stores them sealed with this device’s hardware keystore.
Patient data is medical data. Everything uploaded is encrypted with a key that never leaves this device, so even Telegram cannot read the contents.
Sign in at my.telegram.org, open “API development tools”, and create an application. Copy the App api_id and App api_hash here.
Open Telegram on another device, go to Settings → Devices → Link Desktop Device, and scan this link.
That number has no Telegram account. Create one in the official Telegram app first, then come back.

Ortho Tips shows a notification while large transfers run, so you can see progress and cancel without keeping the app open.\n\nAndroid will ask for permission the first time a transfer starts. Declining is fine — synchronisation still works, you just will not see progress.
Ortho Tips will look for an existing “Ortho Tips Drive” channel on your account and create a private one if there is none. It is never public and has no members other than you.
Confirms this device has room for the local cache and prepares the encryption key used for uploads.
Checks that Telegram accepts uploads from this account and reports the per-file size limit that applies to you.
Every object in the drive carries its own description, so Ortho Tips can tell what is already there without any record on this device. This is what makes the drive a real backup rather than a mirror.
Your existing patient media and records will be queued for upload. Local copies stay exactly where they are — nothing is moved or removed.
